model.title: Earned Wage Access Consumer Protection Act
model.meta: Financial Services Committee · Rep. Bryan Steil (R-WI)

summary.text: The bill would regulate earned wage access products, which let workers get their earned pay before their scheduled payday. It would exempt these products from the Truth in Lending Act's disclosure rules. Providers would have to offer a no-cost way to receive wages if they charge a fee for faster access, and they would be barred from civil suits or collection efforts to force repayment except in cases of fraud. They would also have to reimburse consumers for overdraft fees caused by the provider's errors, disclose all fees and consumer rights before an agreement, and avoid sharing fees or tips with employers. The bill would further limit accepted payment methods and certain fees for non-payment, and bar setting a default tip above $0.
